content:
Stop bringing meaningless offerings!
    Your incense is detestable to me.
  New Moons, Sabbaths and convocations—
    I cannot bear your worthless assemblies.

When you spread out your hands in prayer,
    I hide my eyes from you;
  even when you offer many prayers,
    I am not listening.
    
  Your hands are full of blood!

I will restore your leaders as in days of old,
    your rulers as at the beginning.
  Afterward you will be called
    the City of Righteousness,
    the Faithful City.”

You will be like an oak with fading leaves,
    like a garden without water.

The mighty man will become tinder
    and his work a spark;
  both will burn together,
    with no one to quench the fire.”

Woe to the sinful nation,
    a people whose guilt is great,
  a brood of evildoers,
    children given to corruption!
  They have forsaken the Lord;
    they have spurned the Holy One of Israel
    and turned their backs on him.

Why should you be beaten anymore?
    Why do you persist in rebellion?
  Your whole head is injured,
    your whole heart afflicted.

From the sole of your foot to the top of your head
    there is no soundness—
  only wounds and welts
    and open sores,
  not cleansed or bandaged
    or soothed with olive oil.

“The multitude of your sacrifices—
    what are they to me?”
    says the Lord.
  “I have more than enough of burnt offerings,
    of rams and the fat of fattened animals;
  I have no pleasure
    in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.

When you come to appear before me,
    who has asked this of you,
    this trampling of my courts?

If you are willing and obedient,
    you will eat the good things of the land;

“You will be ashamed because of the sacred oaks
    in which you have delighted;
  you will be disgraced because of the gardens
    that you have chosen.

Hear me, you heavens! Listen, earth!
    For the Lord has spoken:
  “I reared children and brought them up,
    but they have rebelled against me.

Your country is desolate,
    your cities burned with fire;
  your fields are being stripped by foreigners
    right before you,
    laid waste as when overthrown by strangers.

Daughter Zion is left
    like a shelter in a vineyard,
  like a hut in a cucumber field,
    like a city under siege.

Hear the word of the Lord,
    you rulers of Sodom;
  listen to the instruction of our God,
    you people of Gomorrah!

Your New Moon feasts and your appointed festivals
    I hate with all my being.
  They have become a burden to me;
    I am weary of bearing them.

Learn to do right; seek justice.
    Defend the oppressed.
  Take up the cause of the fatherless;
    plead the case of the widow.

See how the faithful city
    has become a prostitute!
  She once was full of justice;
    righteousness used to dwell in her—
    but now murderers!

Your silver has become dross,
    your choice wine is diluted with water.

Zion will be delivered with justice,
    her penitent ones with righteousness.

But rebels and sinners will both be broken,
    and those who forsake the Lord will perish.
The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

The ox knows its master,
    the donkey its owner’s manger,
  but Israel does not know,
    my people do not understand.”

Unless the Lord Almighty
    had left us some survivors,
  we would have become like Sodom,
    we would have been like Gomorrah.

“Come now, let us settle the matter,”
    says the Lord.
  “Though your sins are like scarlet,
    they shall be as white as snow;
  though they are red as crimson,
    they shall be like wool.

but if you resist and rebel,
    you will be devoured by the sword.”
  For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

Therefore the Lord, the Lord Almighty,
    the Mighty One of Israel, declares:
  “Ah! I will vent my wrath on my foes
    and avenge myself on my enemies.

But this is not what he intends,
    this is not what he has in mind;
  his purpose is to destroy,
    to put an end to many nations.

to deprive the poor of their rights
    and withhold justice from the oppressed of my people,
  making widows their prey
    and robbing the fatherless.

Nothing will remain but to cringe among the captives
    or fall among the slain.
    
  Yet for all this, his anger is not turned away,
    his hand is still upraised.

‘Has not Kalno fared like Carchemish?
  Is not Hamath like Arpad,
    and Samaria like Damascus?

Though your people be like the sand by the sea, Israel,
    only a remnant will return.
  Destruction has been decreed,
    overwhelming and righteous.

The Lord, the Lord Almighty, will carry out
    the destruction decreed upon the whole land.

Very soon my anger against you will end
    and my wrath will be directed to their destruction.”

Cry out, Daughter Gallim!
    Listen, Laishah!
    Poor Anathoth!

As my hand seized the kingdoms of the idols,
    kingdoms whose images excelled those of Jerusalem and Samaria—

Does the ax raise itself above the person who swings it,
    or the saw boast against the one who uses it?
  As if a rod were to wield the person who lifts it up,
    or a club brandish the one who is not wood!

Therefore, the Lord, the Lord Almighty,
    will send a wasting disease upon his sturdy warriors;
  under his pomp a fire will be kindled
    like a blazing flame.

And the remaining trees of his forests will be so few
    that a child could write them down.

The Lord Almighty will lash them with a whip,
    as when he struck down Midian at the rock of Oreb;
  and he will raise his staff over the waters,
    as he did in Egypt.

They go over the pass, and say,
    “We will camp overnight at Geba.”
  Ramah trembles;
    Gibeah of Saul flees.

He will cut down the forest thickets with an ax;
    Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.

I send him against a godless nation,
    I dispatch him against a people who anger me,
  to seize loot and snatch plunder,
    and to trample them down like mud in the streets.

shall I not deal with Jerusalem and her images
    as I dealt with Samaria and her idols?’ ”
When the Lord has finished all his work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, he will say, “I will punish the king of Assyria for the willful pride of his heart and the haughty look in his eyes.

The splendor of his forests and fertile fields
    it will completely destroy,
    as when a sick person wastes away.

Therefore this is what the Lord, the Lord Almighty, says:
  “My people who live in Zion,
    do not be afraid of the Assyrians,
  who beat you with a rod
    and lift up a club against you, as Egypt did.

In that day their burden will be lifted from your shoulders,
    their yoke from your neck;
  the yoke will be broken
    because you have grown so fat.

See, the Lord, the Lord Almighty,
    will lop off the boughs with great power.
  The lofty trees will be felled,
    the tall ones will be brought low.

Woe to those who make unjust laws,
    to those who issue oppressive decrees,

What will you do on the day of reckoning,
    when disaster comes from afar?
  To whom will you run for help?
    Where will you leave your riches?

“Woe to the Assyrian, the rod of my anger,
    in whose hand is the club of my wrath!
‘Are not my commanders all kings?’ he says.

For he says:
  “ ‘By the strength of my hand I have done this,
    and by my wisdom, because I have understanding.
  I removed the boundaries of nations,
    I plundered their treasures;
    like a mighty one I subdued their kings.

The Light of Israel will become a fire,
    their Holy One a flame;
  in a single day it will burn and consume
    his thorns and his briers.

In that day the remnant of Israel,
    the survivors of Jacob,
  will no longer rely on him
    who struck them down
  but will truly rely on the Lord,
    the Holy One of Israel.

A remnant will return, a remnant of Jacob
    will return to the Mighty God.

Madmenah is in flight;
    the people of Gebim take cover.

This day they will halt at Nob;
    they will shake their fist
  at the mount of Daughter Zion,
    at the hill of Jerusalem.

A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse;
    from his roots a Branch will bear fruit.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
The Spirit of the Lord will rest on him—
    the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding,
    the Spirit of counsel and of might,
    the Spirit of the knowledge and fear of the Lord—

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content: In that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations will rally to him, and his resting place will be glorious.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
Ephraim’s jealousy will vanish,
    and Judah’s enemies will be destroyed;
  Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah,
    nor Judah hostile toward Ephraim.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
They will swoop down on the slopes of Philistia to the west;
    together they will plunder the people to the east.
  They will subdue Edom and Moab,
    and the Ammonites will be subject to them.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
There will be a highway for the remnant of his people
    that is left from Assyria,
  as there was for Israel
    when they came up from Egypt.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
but with righteousness he will judge the needy,
    with justice he will give decisions for the poor of the earth.
  He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth;
    with the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
The Lord will dry up
    the gulf of the Egyptian sea;
  with a scorching wind he will sweep his hand
    over the Euphrates River.
  He will break it up into seven streams
    so that anyone can cross over in sandals.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
The wolf will live with the lamb,
    the leopard will lie down with the goat,
  the calf and the lion and the yearling together;
    and a little child will lead them.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
They will neither harm nor destroy
    on all my holy mountain,
  for the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord
    as the waters cover the sea.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King
Person and Power of the King

content:
Righteousness will be his belt
    and faithfulness the sash around his waist.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
The cow will feed with the bear,
    their young will lie down together,
    and the lion will eat straw like the ox.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
The infant will play near the cobra’s den,
    and the young child will put its hand into the viper’s nest.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content: In that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the surviving remnant of his people from Assyria, from Lower Egypt, from Upper Egypt, from Cush, from Elam, from Babylonia, from Hamath and from the islands of the Mediterranean.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
He will raise a banner for the nations
    and gather the exiles of Israel;
  he will assemble the scattered people of Judah
    from the four quarters of the earth.

teaching.name: Person and Power of the King

content:
In that day you will say:
  “Give praise to the Lord, proclaim his name;
    make known among the nations what he has done,
    and proclaim that his name is exalted.

With joy you will draw water
    from the wells of salvation.

Sing to the Lord, for he has done glorious things;
    let this be known to all the world.

Shout aloud and sing for joy, people of Zion,
    for great is the Holy One of Israel among you.”

In that day you will say:
  “I will praise you, Lord.
    Although you were angry with me,
  your anger has turned away
    and you have comforted me.

Raise a banner on a bare hilltop,
    shout to them;
  beckon to them
    to enter the gates of the nobles.

Listen, a noise on the mountains,
    like that of a great multitude!
  Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms,
    like nations massing together!
  The Lord Almighty is mustering
    an army for war.

Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms,
    the pride and glory of the Babylonians,
  will be overthrown by God
    like Sodom and Gomorrah.

She will never be inhabited
    or lived in through all generations;
  there no nomads will pitch their tents,
    there no shepherds will rest their flocks.

Terror will seize them,
    pain and anguish will grip them;
    they will writhe like a woman in labor.
  They will look aghast at each other,
    their faces aflame.

The stars of heaven and their constellations
    will not show their light.
  The rising sun will be darkened
    and the moon will not give its light.

Whoever is captured will be thrust through;
    all who are caught will fall by the sword.

But desert creatures will lie there,
    jackals will fill her houses;
  there the owls will dwell,
    and there the wild goats will leap about.

Hyenas will inhabit her strongholds,
    jackals her luxurious palaces.
  Her time is at hand,
    and her days will not be prolonged.

They come from faraway lands,
    from the ends of the heavens—
  the Lord and the weapons of his wrath—
    to destroy the whole country.

See, the day of the Lord is coming
    —a cruel day, with wrath and fierce anger—
  to make the land desolate
    and destroy the sinners within it.

Therefore I will make the heavens tremble;
    and the earth will shake from its place
  at the wrath of the Lord Almighty,
    in the day of his burning anger.

Like a hunted gazelle,
    like sheep without a shepherd,
  they will all return to their own people,
    they will flee to their native land.

Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes;
    their houses will be looted and their wives violated.

See, I will stir up against them the Medes,
    who do not care for silver
    and have no delight in gold.
A prophecy against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw:

Wail, for the day of the Lord is near;
    it will come like destruction from the Almighty.

Because of this, all hands will go limp,
    every heart will melt with fear.

I will punish the world for its evil,
    the wicked for their sins.
  I will put an end to the arrogance of the haughty
    and will humble the pride of the ruthless.

I will make people scarcer than pure gold,
    more rare than the gold of Ophir.

Nations will take them
    and bring them to their own place.
  And Israel will take possession of the nations
    and make them male and female servants in the Lord’s land.
  They will make captives of their captors
    and rule over their oppressors.
On the day the Lord gives you relief from your suffering and turmoil and from the harsh labor forced on you,

All the kings of the nations lie in state,
    each in his own tomb.

The Lord will have compassion on Jacob;
    once again he will choose Israel
    and will settle them in their own land.
  Foreigners will join them
    and unite with the descendants of Jacob.

The Lord has broken the rod of the wicked,
    the scepter of the rulers,

I will ascend above the tops of the clouds;
    I will make myself like the Most High.”

Those who see you stare at you,
    they ponder your fate:
  “Is this the man who shook the earth
    and made kingdoms tremble,

But you are cast out of your tomb
    like a rejected branch;
  you are covered with the slain,
    with those pierced by the sword,
    those who descend to the stones of the pit.
  Like a corpse trampled underfoot,

The poorest of the poor will find pasture,
    and the needy will lie down in safety.
  But your root I will destroy by famine;
    it will slay your survivors.

you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon:
  How the oppressor has come to an end!
    How his fury has ended!

All the lands are at rest and at peace;
    they break into singing.

Even the junipers and the cedars of Lebanon
    gloat over you and say,
  “Now that you have been laid low,
    no one comes to cut us down.”

They will all respond,
    they will say to you,
  “You also have become weak, as we are;
    you have become like us.”

But you are brought down to the realm of the dead,
    to the depths of the pit.

“I will turn her into a place for owls
    and into swampland;
  I will sweep her with the broom of destruction,”
    declares the Lord Almighty.

The Lord Almighty has sworn,
  “Surely, as I have planned, so it will be,
    and as I have purposed, so it will happen.
This prophecy came in the year King Ahaz died:

What answer shall be given
    to the envoys of that nation?
  “The Lord has established Zion,
    and in her his afflicted people will find refuge.”

which in anger struck down peoples
    with unceasing blows,
  and in fury subdued nations
    with relentless aggression.

All your pomp has been brought down to the grave,
    along with the noise of your harps;
  maggots are spread out beneath you
    and worms cover you.

How you have fallen from heaven,
    morning star, son of the dawn!
  You have been cast down to the earth,
    you who once laid low the nations!

the man who made the world a wilderness,
    who overthrew its cities
    and would not let his captives go home?”

you will not join them in burial,
  for you have destroyed your land
    and killed your people.
    
    
  Let the offspring of the wicked
    never be mentioned again.

Prepare a place to slaughter his children
    for the sins of their ancestors;
  they are not to rise to inherit the land
    and cover the earth with their cities.

“I will rise up against them,”
    declares the Lord Almighty.
  “I will wipe out Babylon’s name and survivors,
    her offspring and descendants,”
    declares the Lord.

I will crush the Assyrian in my land;
    on my mountains I will trample him down.
  His yoke will be taken from my people,
    and his burden removed from their shoulders.”

This is the plan determined for the whole world;
    this is the hand stretched out over all nations.

For the Lord Almighty has purposed, and who can thwart him?
    His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?

Wail, you gate! Howl, you city!
    Melt away, all you Philistines!
  A cloud of smoke comes from the north,
    and there is not a straggler in its ranks.

In the streets they wear sackcloth;
    on the roofs and in the public squares
  they all wail,
    prostrate with weeping.

Dibon goes up to its temple,
    to its high places to weep;
    Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba.
  Every head is shaved
    and every beard cut off.

Heshbon and Elealeh cry out,
    their voices are heard all the way to Jahaz.
  Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out,
    and their hearts are faint.

The waters of Nimrim are dried up
    and the grass is withered;
  the vegetation is gone
    and nothing green is left.

The waters of Dimon are full of blood,
    but I will bring still more upon Dimon—
  a lion upon the fugitives of Moab
    and upon those who remain in the land.

A prophecy against Moab:
  Ar in Moab is ruined,
    destroyed in a night!
  Kir in Moab is ruined,
    destroyed in a night!

My heart cries out over Moab;
    her fugitives flee as far as Zoar,
    as far as Eglath Shelishiyah.
  They go up the hill to Luhith,
    weeping as they go;
  on the road to Horonaim
    they lament their destruction.

So the wealth they have acquired and stored up
    they carry away over the Ravine of the Poplars.
This is the word the Lord has already spoken concerning Moab.

Send lambs as tribute
    to the ruler of the land,
  from Sela, across the desert,
    to the mount of Daughter Zion.

In love a throne will be established;
    in faithfulness a man will sit on it—
    one from the house of David—
  one who in judging seeks justice
    and speeds the cause of righteousness.

We have heard of Moab’s pride—
    how great is her arrogance!—
  of her conceit, her pride and her insolence;
    but her boasts are empty.

So I weep, as Jazer weeps,
    for the vines of Sibmah.
  Heshbon and Elealeh,
    I drench you with tears!
  The shouts of joy over your ripened fruit
    and over your harvests have been stilled.

My heart laments for Moab like a harp,
    my inmost being for Kir Hareseth.

When Moab appears at her high place,
    she only wears herself out;
  when she goes to her shrine to pray,
    it is to no avail.
But now the Lord says: “Within three years, as a servant bound by contract would count them, Moab’s splendor and all her many people will be despised, and her survivors will be very few and feeble.”

Like fluttering birds
    pushed from the nest,
  so are the women of Moab
    at the fords of the Arnon.

“Make up your mind,” Moab says.
    “Render a decision.
  Make your shadow like night—
    at high noon.
  Hide the fugitives,
    do not betray the refugees.

Therefore the Moabites wail,
    they wail together for Moab.
  Lament and grieve
    for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth.

The fields of Heshbon wither,
    the vines of Sibmah also.
  The rulers of the nations
    have trampled down the choicest vines,
  which once reached Jazer
    and spread toward the desert.
  Their shoots spread out
    and went as far as the sea.

In that day people will look to their Maker
    and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
You have forgotten God your Savior;
    you have not remembered the Rock, your fortress.
  Therefore, though you set out the finest plants
    and plant imported vines,

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
Although the peoples roar like the roar of surging waters,
    when he rebukes them they flee far away,
  driven before the wind like chaff on the hills,
    like tumbleweed before a gale.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
A prophecy against Damascus:
  “See, Damascus will no longer be a city
    but will become a heap of ruins.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
The cities of Aroer will be deserted
    and left to flocks, which will lie down,
    with no one to make them afraid.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
Yet some gleanings will remain,
    as when an olive tree is beaten,
  leaving two or three olives on the topmost branches,
    four or five on the fruitful boughs,”
    declares the Lord, the God of Israel.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content: In that day their strong cities, which they left because of the Israelites, will be like places abandoned to thickets and undergrowth. And all will be desolation.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
Woe to the many nations that rage—
    they rage like the raging sea!
  Woe to the peoples who roar—
    they roar like the roaring of great waters!

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
The fortified city will disappear from Ephraim,
    and royal power from Damascus;
  the remnant of Aram will be
    like the glory of the Israelites,”
    declares the Lord Almighty.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
“In that day the glory of Jacob will fade;
    the fat of his body will waste away.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
They will not look to the altars,
    the work of their hands,
  and they will have no regard for the Asherah poles
    and the incense altars their fingers have made.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
though on the day you set them out, you make them grow,
    and on the morning when you plant them, you bring them to bud,
  yet the harvest will be as nothing
    in the day of disease and incurable pain.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
It will be as when reapers harvest the standing grain,
    gathering the grain in their arms—
  as when someone gleans heads of grain
    in the Valley of Rephaim.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
In the evening, sudden terror!
    Before the morning, they are gone!
  This is the portion of those who loot us,
    the lot of those who plunder us.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush
The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
Woe to the land of whirring wings
    along the rivers of Cush,

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
All you people of the world,
    you who live on the earth,
  when a banner is raised on the mountains,
    you will see it,
  and when a trumpet sounds,
    you will hear it.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
which sends envoys by sea
    in papyrus boats over the water.
    
  Go, swift messengers,
  to a people tall and smooth-skinned,
    to a people feared far and wide,
  an aggressive nation of strange speech,
    whose land is divided by rivers.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
This is what the Lord says to me:
    “I will remain quiet and will look on from my dwelling place,
  like shimmering heat in the sunshine,
    like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
For, before the harvest, when the blossom is gone
    and the flower becomes a ripening grape,
  he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives,
    and cut down and take away the spreading branches.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey
    and to the wild animals;
  the birds will feed on them all summer,
    the wild animals all winter.

teaching.name: The Burdens of Damascus and Cush

content:
A prophecy against Egypt:
  See, the Lord rides on a swift cloud
    and is coming to Egypt.
  The idols of Egypt tremble before him,
    and the hearts of the Egyptians melt with fear.

Those who work with combed flax will despair,
    the weavers of fine linen will lose hope.

The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools;
    the wise counselors of Pharaoh give senseless advice.
  How can you say to Pharaoh,
    “I am one of the wise men,
    a disciple of the ancient kings”?

There is nothing Egypt can do—
    head or tail, palm branch or reed.
The Lord will strike Egypt with a plague; he will strike them and heal them. They will turn to the Lord, and he will respond to their pleas and heal them.
The Lord Almighty will bless them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria my handiwork, and Israel my inheritance.”

“I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian—
    brother will fight against brother,
    neighbor against neighbor,
    city against city,
    kingdom against kingdom.

The fishermen will groan and lament,
    all who cast hooks into the Nile;
  those who throw nets on the water
    will pine away.

Where are your wise men now?
    Let them show you and make known
  what the Lord Almighty
    has planned against Egypt.
And the land of Judah will bring terror to the Egyptians; everyone to whom Judah is mentioned will be terrified, because of what the Lord Almighty is planning against them.
In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the heart of Egypt, and a monument to the Lord at its border.
It will be a sign and witness to the Lord Almighty in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the Lord because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, and he will rescue them.

So the Lord will make himself known to the Egyptians, and in that day they will acknowledge the Lord. They will worship with sacrifices and grain offerings; they will make vows to the Lord and keep them.

I will hand the Egyptians over
    to the power of a cruel master,
  and a fierce king will rule over them,”
    declares the Lord, the Lord Almighty.

The waters of the river will dry up,
    and the riverbed will be parched and dry.

The workers in cloth will be dejected,
    and all the wage earners will be sick at heart.

The officials of Zoan have become fools,
    the leaders of Memphis are deceived;
  the cornerstones of her peoples
    have led Egypt astray.

The Lord has poured into them
    a spirit of dizziness;
  they make Egypt stagger in all that she does,
    as a drunkard staggers around in his vomit.
In that day the Egyptians will become weaklings. They will shudder with fear at the uplifted hand that the Lord Almighty raises against them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
In that day Israel will be the third, along with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing on the earth.

The Egyptians will lose heart,
    and I will bring their plans to nothing;
  they will consult the idols and the spirits of the dead,
    the mediums and the spiritists.

also the plants along the Nile,
    at the mouth of the river.
  Every sown field along the Nile
    will become parched, will blow away and be no more.
In that day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord Almighty. One of them will be called the City of the Sun.
This is what Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
He will judge between the nations
    and will settle disputes for many peoples.
  They will beat their swords into plowshares
    and their spears into pruning hooks.
  Nation will not take up sword against nation,
    nor will they train for war anymore.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
In that day people will throw away
    to the moles and bats
  their idols of silver and idols of gold,
    which they made to worship.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
Many peoples will come and say,
  “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord,
    to the temple of the God of Jacob.
  He will teach us his ways,
    so that we may walk in his paths.”
  The law will go out from Zion,
    the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
So people will be brought low
    and everyone humbled—
    do not forgive them.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
for every lofty tower
    and every fortified wall,

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
for every trading ship
    and every stately vessel.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content: and the idols will totally disappear.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
They will flee to caverns in the rocks
    and to the overhanging crags
  from the fearful presence of the Lord
    and the splendor of his majesty,
    when he rises to shake the earth.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
Come, descendants of Jacob,
    let us walk in the light of the Lord.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel
Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel
Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
The Lord Almighty has a day in store
    for all the proud and lofty,
  for all that is exalted
    (and they will be humbled),

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
for all the cedars of Lebanon, tall and lofty,
    and all the oaks of Bashan,

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel
Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
People will flee to caves in the rocks
    and to holes in the ground
  from the fearful presence of the Lord
    and the splendor of his majesty,
    when he rises to shake the earth.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
In the last days
  the mountain of the Lord’s temple will be established
    as the highest of the mountains;
  it will be exalted above the hills,
    and all nations will stream to it.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
You, Lord, have abandoned your people,
    the descendants of Jacob.
  They are full of superstitions from the East;
    they practice divination like the Philistines
    and embrace pagan customs.

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel
Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
Go into the rocks, hide in the ground
    from the fearful presence of the Lord
    and the splendor of his majesty!

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
for all the towering mountains
    and all the high hills,

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content:
Stop trusting in mere humans,
    who have but a breath in their nostrils.
    Why hold them in esteem?

teaching.name: Prophecy concerning the last days of Israel

content: In the year that the supreme commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it—
at that time the Lord spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz. He said to him, “Take off the sackcloth from your body and the sandals from your feet.” And he did so, going around stripped and barefoot.
Those who trusted in Cush and boasted in Egypt will be dismayed and put to shame.
In that day the people who live on this coast will say, ‘See what has happened to those we relied on, those we fled to for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’ ”
Then the Lord said, “Just as my servant Isaiah has gone stripped and barefoot for three years, as a sign and portent against Egypt and Cush,
so the king of Assyria will lead away stripped and barefoot the Egyptian captives and Cushite exiles, young and old, with buttocks bared—to Egypt’s shame.

A dire vision has been shown to me:
    The traitor betrays, the looter takes loot.
  Elam, attack! Media, lay siege!
    I will bring to an end all the groaning she caused.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
My heart falters,
    fear makes me tremble;
  the twilight I longed for
    has become a horror to me.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
A prophecy against Arabia:
  You caravans of Dedanites,
    who camp in the thickets of Arabia,

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
They set the tables,
    they spread the rugs,
    they eat, they drink!
  Get up, you officers,
    oil the shields!

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
When he sees chariots
    with teams of horses,
  riders on donkeys
    or riders on camels,
  let him be alert,
    fully alert.”

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia
Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
My people who are crushed on the threshing floor,
    I tell you what I have heard
  from the Lord Almighty,
    from the God of Israel.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
They flee from the sword,
    from the drawn sword,
  from the bent bow
    and from the heat of battle.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
This is what the Lord says to me:
  “Go, post a lookout
    and have him report what he sees.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
Look, here comes a man in a chariot
    with a team of horses.
  And he gives back the answer:
    ‘Babylon has fallen, has fallen!
  All the images of its gods
    lie shattered on the ground!’ ”

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
The watchman replies,
    “Morning is coming, but also the night.
  If you would ask, then ask;
    and come back yet again.”

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
A prophecy against the Desert by the Sea:
  Like whirlwinds sweeping through the southland,
    an invader comes from the desert,
    from a land of terror.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
At this my body is racked with pain,
    pangs seize me, like those of a woman in labor;
  I am staggered by what I hear,
    I am bewildered by what I see.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
A prophecy against Dumah:
  Someone calls to me from Seir,
    “Watchman, what is left of the night?
    Watchman, what is left of the night?”

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia
Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content: This is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a servant bound by contract would count it, all the splendor of Kedar will come to an end.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content: The survivors of the archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” The Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.

teaching.name: Three Burdens: Babylon, Edom and Arabia

content:
A prophecy against the Valley of Vision:
  What troubles you now,
    that you have all gone up on the roofs,

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
you town so full of commotion,
    you city of tumult and revelry?
  Your slain were not killed by the sword,
    nor did they die in battle.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision
The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
The Lord stripped away the defenses of Judah,
    and you looked in that day
    to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
Therefore I said, “Turn away from me;
    let me weep bitterly.
  Do not try to console me
    over the destruction of my people.”

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
Your choicest valleys are full of chariots,
    and horsemen are posted at the city gates.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
All your leaders have fled together;
    they have been captured without using the bow.
  All you who were caught were taken prisoner together,
    having fled while the enemy was still far away.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
The Lord, the Lord Almighty, has a day
    of tumult and trampling and terror
    in the Valley of Vision,
  a day of battering down walls
    and of crying out to the mountains.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
You saw that the walls of the City of David
    were broken through in many places;
  you stored up water
    in the Lower Pool.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
You counted the buildings in Jerusalem
    and tore down houses to strengthen the wall.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
You built a reservoir between the two walls
    for the water of the Old Pool,
  but you did not look to the One who made it,
    or have regard for the One who planned it long ago.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
He will roll you up tightly like a ball
    and throw you into a large country.
  There you will die
    and there the chariots you were so proud of
    will become a disgrace to your master’s house.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: The Lord Almighty has revealed this in my hearing: “Till your dying day this sin will not be atoned for,” says the Lord, the Lord Almighty.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
This is what the Lord, the Lord Almighty, says:
  “Go, say to this steward,
    to Shebna the palace administrator:

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
What are you doing here and who gave you permission
    to cut out a grave for yourself here,
  hewing your grave on the height
    and chiseling your resting place in the rock?

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
The Lord, the Lord Almighty,
    called you on that day
  to weep and to wail,
    to tear out your hair and put on sackcloth.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
But see, there is joy and revelry,
    slaughtering of cattle and killing of sheep,
    eating of meat and drinking of wine!
  “Let us eat and drink,” you say,
    “for tomorrow we die!”

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
“Beware, the Lord is about to take firm hold of you
    and hurl you away, you mighty man.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
I will depose you from your office,
    and you will be ousted from your position.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him and hand your authority over to him. He will be a father to those who live in Jerusalem and to the people of Judah.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David; what he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place; he will become a seat of honor for the house of his father.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: “In that day I will summon my servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: All the glory of his family will hang on him: its offspring and offshoots—all its lesser vessels, from the bowls to all the jars.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content: “In that day,” declares the Lord Almighty, “the peg driven into the firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and will fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut down.” The Lord has spoken.

teaching.name: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

content:
A prophecy against Tyre:
  Wail, you ships of Tarshish!
    For Tyre is destroyed
    and left without house or harbor.
  From the land of Cyprus
    word has come to them.

When word comes to Egypt,
    they will be in anguish at the report from Tyre.

Cross over to Tarshish;
    wail, you people of the island.

Who planned this against Tyre,
    the bestower of crowns,
  whose merchants are princes,
    whose traders are renowned in the earth?

Till your land as they do along the Nile,
    Daughter Tarshish,
    for you no longer have a harbor.

On the great waters
    came the grain of the Shihor;
  the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre,
    and she became the marketplace of the nations.

Is this your city of revelry,
    the old, old city,
  whose feet have taken her
    to settle in far-off lands?

The Lord has stretched out his hand over the sea
    and made its kingdoms tremble.
  He has given an order concerning Phoenicia
    that her fortresses be destroyed.

Wail, you ships of Tarshish;
    your fortress is destroyed!
At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the span of a king’s life. But at the end of these seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:

“Take up a harp, walk through the city,
    you forgotten prostitute;
  play the harp well, sing many a song,
    so that you will be remembered.”
Yet her profit and her earnings will be set apart for the Lord; they will not be stored up or hoarded. Her profits will go to those who live before the Lord, for abundant food and fine clothes.

He said, “No more of your reveling,
    Virgin Daughter Sidon, now crushed!
    
  “Up, cross over to Cyprus;
    even there you will find no rest.”

Look at the land of the Babylonians,
    this people that is now of no account!
  The Assyrians have made it
    a place for desert creatures;
  they raised up their siege towers,
    they stripped its fortresses bare
    and turned it into a ruin.

Be silent, you people of the island
    and you merchants of Sidon,
    whom the seafarers have enriched.

The Lord Almighty planned it,
    to bring down her pride in all her splendor
    and to humble all who are renowned on the earth.
At the end of seventy years, the Lord will deal with Tyre. She will return to her lucrative prostitution and will ply her trade with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.

The earth dries up and withers,
    the world languishes and withers,
    the heavens languish with the earth.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The ruined city lies desolate;
    the entrance to every house is barred.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
No longer do they drink wine with a song;
    the beer is bitter to its drinkers.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation
The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
Terror and pit and snare await you,
    people of the earth.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
Whoever flees at the sound of terror
    will fall into a pit;
  whoever climbs out of the pit
    will be caught in a snare.
    
  The floodgates of the heavens are opened,
    the foundations of the earth shake.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The earth reels like a drunkard,
    it sways like a hut in the wind;
  so heavy upon it is the guilt of its rebellion
    that it falls—never to rise again.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
In that day the Lord will punish
    the powers in the heavens above
    and the kings on the earth below.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
See, the Lord is going to lay waste the earth
    and devastate it;
  he will ruin its face
    and scatter its inhabitants—

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation
The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
Therefore a curse consumes the earth;
    its people must bear their guilt.
  Therefore earth’s inhabitants are burned up,
    and very few are left.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The joyful timbrels are stilled,
    the noise of the revelers has stopped,
    the joyful harp is silent.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The city is left in ruins,
    its gate is battered to pieces.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
They raise their voices, they shout for joy;
    from the west they acclaim the Lord’s majesty.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation
The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The earth is broken up,
    the earth is split asunder,
    the earth is violently shaken.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
They will be herded together
    like prisoners bound in a dungeon;
  they will be shut up in prison
    and be punished after many days.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The moon will be dismayed,
    the sun ashamed;
  for the Lord Almighty will reign
    on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
    and before its elders—with great glory.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The earth will be completely laid waste
    and totally plundered.
  The Lord has spoken this word.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The earth is defiled by its people;
    they have disobeyed the laws,
  violated the statutes
    and broken the everlasting covenant.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
The new wine dries up and the vine withers;
    all the merrymakers groan.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
So will it be on the earth
    and among the nations,
  as when an olive tree is beaten,
    or as when gleanings are left after the grape harvest.

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
From the ends of the earth we hear singing:
    “Glory to the Righteous One.”
    
  But I said, “I waste away, I waste away!
    Woe to me!
  The treacherous betray!
    With treachery the treacherous betray!”

teaching.name: The Coming of the Great Tribulation

content:
Lord, you are my God;
    I will exalt you and praise your name,
  for in perfect faithfulness
    you have done wonderful things,
    things planned long ago.

You have made the city a heap of rubble,
    the fortified town a ruin,
  the foreigners’ stronghold a city no more;
    it will never be rebuilt.

You have been a refuge for the poor,
    a refuge for the needy in their distress,
  a shelter from the storm
    and a shade from the heat.
  For the breath of the ruthless
    is like a storm driving against a wall

he will swallow up death forever.
  The Sovereign Lord will wipe away the tears
    from all faces;
  he will remove his people’s disgrace
    from all the earth.
  The Lord has spoken.

They will stretch out their hands in it,
    as swimmers stretch out their hands to swim.
  God will bring down their pride
    despite the cleverness of their hands.

Therefore strong peoples will honor you;
    cities of ruthless nations will revere you.

He will bring down your high fortified walls
    and lay them low;
  he will bring them down to the ground,
    to the very dust.

and like the heat of the desert.
  You silence the uproar of foreigners;
    as heat is reduced by the shadow of a cloud,
    so the song of the ruthless is stilled.

On this mountain the Lord Almighty will prepare
    a feast of rich food for all peoples,
  a banquet of aged wine—
    the best of meats and the finest of wines.

In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah:
  We have a strong city;
    God makes salvation
    its walls and ramparts.

Yes, Lord, walking in the way of your laws,
    we wait for you;
  your name and renown
    are the desire of our hearts.

Lord, you establish peace for us;
    all that we have accomplished you have done for us.

As a pregnant woman about to give birth
    writhes and cries out in her pain,
    so were we in your presence, Lord.

Open the gates
    that the righteous nation may enter,
    the nation that keeps faith.

Trust in the Lord forever,
    for the Lord, the Lord himself, is the Rock eternal.

Feet trample it down—
    the feet of the oppressed,
    the footsteps of the poor.

Lord our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us,
    but your name alone do we honor.

My soul yearns for you in the night;
    in the morning my spirit longs for you.
  When your judgments come upon the earth,
    the people of the world learn righteousness.

We were with child, we writhed in labor,
    but we gave birth to wind.
  We have not brought salvation to the earth,
    and the people of the world have not come to life.

Go, my people, enter your rooms
    and shut the doors behind you;
  hide yourselves for a little while
    until his wrath has passed by.

You will keep in perfect peace
    those whose minds are steadfast,
    because they trust in you.

He humbles those who dwell on high,
    he lays the lofty city low;
  he levels it to the ground
    and casts it down to the dust.

The path of the righteous is level;
    you, the Upright One, make the way of the righteous smooth.

But when grace is shown to the wicked,
    they do not learn righteousness;
  even in a land of uprightness they go on doing evil
    and do not regard the majesty of the Lord.

Lord, your hand is lifted high,
    but they do not see it.
  Let them see your zeal for your people and be put to shame;
    let the fire reserved for your enemies consume them.

See, the Lord is coming out of his dwelling
    to punish the people of the earth for their sins.
  The earth will disclose the blood shed on it;
    the earth will conceal its slain no longer.

I am not angry.
  If only there were briers and thorns confronting me!
    I would march against them in battle;
    I would set them all on fire.

In days to come Jacob will take root,
    Israel will bud and blossom
    and fill all the world with fruit.

When its twigs are dry, they are broken off
    and women come and make fires with them.
  For this is a people without understanding;
    so their Maker has no compassion on them,
    and their Creator shows them no favor.

In that day,
  the Lord will punish with his sword—
    his fierce, great and powerful sword—
  Leviathan the gliding serpent,
    Leviathan the coiling serpent;
  he will slay the monster of the sea.

By warfare and exile you contend with her—
    with his fierce blast he drives her out,
    as on a day the east wind blows.

By this, then, will Jacob’s guilt be atoned for,
    and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin:
  When he makes all the altar stones
    to be like limestone crushed to pieces,
  no Asherah poles or incense altars
    will be left standing.
And in that day a great trumpet will sound. Those who were perishing in Assyria and those who were exiled in Egypt will come and worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

In that day—
  “Sing about a fruitful vineyard:

Has the Lord struck her
    as he struck down those who struck her?
  Has she been killed
    as those were killed who killed her?

I, the Lord, watch over it;
    I water it continually.
  I guard it day and night
    so that no one may harm it.
In that day the Lord will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, Israel, will be gathered up one by one.

See, the Lord has one who is powerful and strong.
    Like a hailstorm and a destructive wind,
  like a driving rain and a flooding downpour,
    he will throw it forcefully to the ground.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
He will be a spirit of justice
    to the one who sits in judgment,
  a source of strength
    to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
And these also stagger from wine
    and reel from beer:
  Priests and prophets stagger from beer
    and are befuddled with wine;
  they reel from beer,
    they stagger when seeing visions,
    they stumble when rendering decisions.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
to whom he said,
    “This is the resting place, let the weary rest”;
  and, “This is the place of repose”—
    but they would not listen.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
I will make justice the measuring line
    and righteousness the plumb line;
  hail will sweep away your refuge, the lie,
    and water will overflow your hiding place.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Now stop your mocking,
    or your chains will become heavier;
  the Lord, the Lord Almighty, has told me
    of the destruction decreed against the whole land.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
When a farmer plows for planting, does he plow continually?
    Does he keep on breaking up and working the soil?

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
When he has leveled the surface,
    does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin?
  Does he not plant wheat in its place,
    barley in its plot,
    and spelt in its field?

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
That fading flower, his glorious beauty,
    set on the head of a fertile valley,
  will be like figs ripe before harvest—
    as soon as people see them and take them in hand,
    they swallow them.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
“Who is it he is trying to teach?
    To whom is he explaining his message?
  To children weaned from their milk,
    to those just taken from the breast?

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
The bed is too short to stretch out on,
    the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Listen and hear my voice;
    pay attention and hear what I say.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Woe to that wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards,
    to the fading flower, his glorious beauty,
  set on the head of a fertile valley—
    to that city, the pride of those laid low by wine!

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
That wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards,
    will be trampled underfoot.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Very well then, with foreign lips and strange tongues
    God will speak to this people,

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you scoffers
    who rule this people in Jerusalem.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Caraway is not threshed with a sledge,
    nor is the wheel of a cart rolled over cumin;
  caraway is beaten out with a rod,
    and cumin with a stick.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
All this also comes from the Lord Almighty,
    whose plan is wonderful,
    whose wisdom is magnificent.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
In that day the Lord Almighty
    will be a glorious crown,
  a beautiful wreath
    for the remnant of his people.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
All the tables are covered with vomit
    and there is not a spot without filth.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
For it is:
    Do this, do that,
    a rule for this, a rule for that;
    a little here, a little there.”

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning
A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
You boast, “We have entered into a covenant with death,
    with the realm of the dead we have made an agreement.
  When an overwhelming scourge sweeps by,
    it cannot touch us,
  for we have made a lie our refuge
    and falsehood our hiding place.”

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
So this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
  “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone,
    a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation;
  the one who relies on it
    will never be stricken with panic.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Your covenant with death will be annulled;
    your agreement with the realm of the dead will not stand.
  When the overwhelming scourge sweeps by,
    you will be beaten down by it.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
As often as it comes it will carry you away;
    morning after morning, by day and by night,
    it will sweep through.”
    
  The understanding of this message
    will bring sheer terror.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
The Lord will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim,
    he will rouse himself as in the Valley of Gibeon—
  to do his work, his strange work,
    and perform his task, his alien task.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
His God instructs him
    and teaches him the right way.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Grain must be ground to make bread;
    so one does not go on threshing it forever.
  The wheels of a threshing cart may be rolled over it,
    but one does not use horses to grind grain.

teaching.name: A picture of the Future and a warning

content:
Woe to you, Ariel, Ariel,
    the city where David settled!
  Add year to year
    and let your cycle of festivals go on.

But your many enemies will become like fine dust,
    the ruthless hordes like blown chaff.
  Suddenly, in an instant,

the Lord Almighty will come
  with thunder and earthquake and great noise,
    with windstorm and tempest and flames of a devouring fire.
Or if you give the scroll to someone who cannot read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I don’t know how to read.”

You turn things upside down,
    as if the potter were thought to be like the clay!
  Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it,
    “You did not make me”?
  Can the pot say to the potter,
    “You know nothing”?

In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll,
    and out of gloom and darkness
    the eyes of the blind will see.

Once more the humble will rejoice in the Lord;
    the needy will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

Then the hordes of all the nations that fight against Ariel,
    that attack her and her fortress and besiege her,
  will be as it is with a dream,
    with a vision in the night—
For you this whole vision is nothing but words sealed in a scroll. And if you give the scroll to someone who can read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I can’t; it is sealed.”

The ruthless will vanish,
    the mockers will disappear,
    and all who have an eye for evil will be cut down—

When they see among them their children,
    the work of my hands,
  they will keep my name holy;
    they will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob,
    and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

Those who are wayward in spirit will gain understanding;
    those who complain will accept instruction.”

Be stunned and amazed,
    blind yourselves and be sightless;
  be drunk, but not from wine,
    stagger, but not from beer.

Therefore once more I will astound these people
    with wonder upon wonder;
  the wisdom of the wise will perish,
    the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish.”

Woe to those who go to great depths
    to hide their plans from the Lord,
  who do their work in darkness and think,
    “Who sees us? Who will know?”

those who with a word make someone out to be guilty,
    who ensnare the defender in court
    and with false testimony deprive the innocent of justice.

as when a hungry person dreams of eating,
    but awakens hungry still;
  as when a thirsty person dreams of drinking,
    but awakens faint and thirsty still.
  So will it be with the hordes of all the nations
    that fight against Mount Zion.

The Lord says:
  “These people come near to me with their mouth
    and honor me with their lips,
    but their hearts are far from me.
  Their worship of me
    is based on merely human rules they have been taught.

In a very short time, will not Lebanon be turned into a fertile field
    and the fertile field seem like a forest?

the captain of fifty and the man of rank,
    the counselor, skilled craftsman and clever enchanter.

A man will seize one of his brothers
    in his father’s house, and say,
  “You have a cloak, you be our leader;
    take charge of this heap of ruins!”

But in that day he will cry out,
    “I have no remedy.
  I have no food or clothing in my house;
    do not make me the leader of the people.”
the fine robes and the capes and cloaks, the purses

Your men will fall by the sword,
    your warriors in battle.

“I will make mere youths their officials;
    children will rule over them.”

People will oppress each other—
    man against man, neighbor against neighbor.
  The young will rise up against the old,
    the nobody against the honored.

Jerusalem staggers,
    Judah is falling;
  their words and deeds are against the Lord,
    defying his glorious presence.

Tell the righteous it will be well with them,
    for they will enjoy the fruit of their deeds.

Woe to the wicked!
    Disaster is upon them!
  They will be paid back
    for what their hands have done.

The Lord enters into judgment
    against the elders and leaders of his people:
  “It is you who have ruined my vineyard;
    the plunder from the poor is in your houses.
In that day the Lord will snatch away their finery: the bangles and headbands and crescent necklaces,
the headdresses and anklets and sashes, the perfume bottles and charms,

Youths oppress my people,
    women rule over them.
  My people, your guides lead you astray;
    they turn you from the path.

The Lord takes his place in court;
    he rises to judge the people.
the earrings and bracelets and veils,
the signet rings and nose rings,
and mirrors, and the linen garments and tiaras and shawls.

The gates of Zion will lament and mourn;
    destitute, she will sit on the ground.

See now, the Lord,
    the Lord Almighty,
  is about to take from Jerusalem and Judah
    both supply and support:
  all supplies of food and all supplies of water,

the hero and the warrior,
  the judge and the prophet,
    the diviner and the elder,

What do you mean by crushing my people
    and grinding the faces of the poor?”
    declares the Lord, the Lord Almighty.

The Lord says,
    “The women of Zion are haughty,
  walking along with outstretched necks,
    flirting with their eyes,
  strutting along with swaying hips,
    with ornaments jingling on their ankles.

Therefore the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the women of Zion;
    the Lord will make their scalps bald.”

“Woe to the obstinate children,”
    declares the Lord,
  “to those who carry out plans that are not mine,
    forming an alliance, but not by my Spirit,
    heaping sin upon sin;

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
But Pharaoh’s protection will be to your shame,
    Egypt’s shade will bring you disgrace.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Though they have officials in Zoan
    and their envoys have arrived in Hanes,

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
A prophecy concerning the animals of the Negev:
  Through a land of hardship and distress,
    of lions and lionesses,
    of adders and darting snakes,
  the envoys carry their riches on donkeys’ backs,
    their treasures on the humps of camels,
  to that unprofitable nation,

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
this sin will become for you
    like a high wall, cracked and bulging,
    that collapses suddenly, in an instant.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: Then you will desecrate your idols overlaid with silver and your images covered with gold; you will throw them away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, “Away with you!”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: In the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every lofty hill.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
And you will sing
    as on the night you celebrate a holy festival;
  your hearts will rejoice
    as when people playing pipes go up
  to the mountain of the Lord,
    to the Rock of Israel.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
everyone will be put to shame
    because of a people useless to them,
  who bring neither help nor advantage,
    but only shame and disgrace.”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Go now, write it on a tablet for them,
    inscribe it on a scroll,
  that for the days to come
    it may be an everlasting witness.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Leave this way,
    get off this path,
  and stop confronting us
    with the Holy One of Israel!”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
You said, ‘No, we will flee on horses.’
    Therefore you will flee!
  You said, ‘We will ride off on swift horses.’
    Therefore your pursuers will be swift!

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Yet the Lord longs to be gracious to you;
    therefore he will rise up to show you compassion.
  For the Lord is a God of justice.
    Blessed are all who wait for him!

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
See, the Name of the Lord comes from afar,
    with burning anger and dense clouds of smoke;
  his lips are full of wrath,
    and his tongue is a consuming fire.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
The Lord will cause people to hear his majestic voice
    and will make them see his arm coming down
  with raging anger and consuming fire,
    with cloudburst, thunderstorm and hail.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
For these are rebellious people, deceitful children,
    children unwilling to listen to the Lord’s instruction.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
They say to the seers,
    “See no more visions!”
  and to the prophets,
    “Give us no more visions of what is right!
  Tell us pleasant things,
    prophesy illusions.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
It will break in pieces like pottery,
    shattered so mercilessly
  that among its pieces not a fragment will be found
    for taking coals from a hearth
    or scooping water out of a cistern.”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
This is what the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says:
  “In repentance and rest is your salvation,
    in quietness and trust is your strength,
    but you would have none of it.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
A thousand will flee
    at the threat of one;
  at the threat of five
    you will all flee away,
  till you are left
    like a flagstaff on a mountaintop,
    like a banner on a hill.”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: He will also send you rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the food that comes from the land will be rich and plentiful. In that day your cattle will graze in broad meadows.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: The moon will shine like the sun, and the sunlight will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, when the Lord binds up the bruises of his people and heals the wounds he inflicted.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
His breath is like a rushing torrent,
    rising up to the neck.
  He shakes the nations in the sieve of destruction;
    he places in the jaws of the peoples
    a bit that leads them astray.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Every stroke the Lord lays on them
    with his punishing club
  will be to the music of timbrels and harps,
    as he fights them in battle with the blows of his arm.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Topheth has long been prepared;
    it has been made ready for the king.
  Its fire pit has been made deep and wide,
    with an abundance of fire and wood;
  the breath of the Lord,
    like a stream of burning sulfur,
    sets it ablaze.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
who go down to Egypt
    without consulting me;
  who look for help to Pharaoh’s protection,
    to Egypt’s shade for refuge.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
to Egypt, whose help is utterly useless.
  Therefore I call her
    Rahab the Do-Nothing.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says:
  “Because you have rejected this message,
    relied on oppression
    and depended on deceit,

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: People of Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. How gracious he will be when you cry for help! As soon as he hears, he will answer you.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: Although the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teachers will be hidden no more; with your own eyes you will see them.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat fodder and mash, spread out with fork and shovel.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
The voice of the Lord will shatter Assyria;
    with his rod he will strike them down.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
This is what the Lord says to me:
  “As a lion growls,
    a great lion over its prey—
  and though a whole band of shepherds
    is called together against it,
  it is not frightened by their shouts
    or disturbed by their clamor—
  so the Lord Almighty will come down
    to do battle on Mount Zion and on its heights.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: Return, you Israelites, to the One you have so greatly revolted against.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Their stronghold will fall because of terror;
    at the sight of the battle standard their commanders will panic,”
  declares the Lord,
    whose fire is in Zion,
    whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Like birds hovering overhead,
    the Lord Almighty will shield Jerusalem;
  he will shield it and deliver it,
    he will ‘pass over’ it and will rescue it.”

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content: For in that day every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold your sinful hands have made.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
“Assyria will fall by no human sword;
    a sword, not of mortals, will devour them.
  They will flee before the sword
    and their young men will be put to forced labor.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
    who rely on horses,
  who trust in the multitude of their chariots
    and in the great strength of their horsemen,
  but do not look to the Holy One of Israel,
    or seek help from the Lord.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
Yet he too is wise and can bring disaster;
    he does not take back his words.
  He will rise up against that wicked nation,
    against those who help evildoers.

teaching.name: Judah to turn to the Lord
Judah to turn to the Lord

content:
No longer will the fool be called noble
    nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
You women who are so complacent,
    rise up and listen to me;
  you daughters who feel secure,
    hear what I have to say!

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
In little more than a year
    you who feel secure will tremble;
  the grape harvest will fail,
    and the harvest of fruit will not come.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Tremble, you complacent women;
    shudder, you daughters who feel secure!
  Strip off your fine clothes
    and wrap yourselves in rags.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields,
    for the fruitful vines

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
till the Spirit is poured on us from on high,
    and the desert becomes a fertile field,
    and the fertile field seems like a forest.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
But the noble make noble plans,
    and by noble deeds they stand.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
and for the land of my people,
    a land overgrown with thorns and briers—
  yes, mourn for all houses of merriment
    and for this city of revelry.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
The Lord’s justice will dwell in the desert,
    his righteousness live in the fertile field.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
how blessed you will be,
    sowing your seed by every stream,
    and letting your cattle and donkeys range free.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind
    and a refuge from the storm,
  like streams of water in the desert
    and the shadow of a great rock in a thirsty land.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed,
    and the ears of those who hear will listen.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
The fearful heart will know and understand,
    and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
For fools speak folly,
    their hearts are bent on evil:
  They practice ungodliness
    and spread error concerning the Lord;
  the hungry they leave empty
    and from the thirsty they withhold water.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Scoundrels use wicked methods,
    they make up evil schemes
  to destroy the poor with lies,
    even when the plea of the needy is just.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
My people will live in peaceful dwelling places,
    in secure homes,
    in undisturbed places of rest.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Though hail flattens the forest
    and the city is leveled completely,

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
See, a king will reign in righteousness
    and rulers will rule with justice.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
The fortress will be abandoned,
    the noisy city deserted;
  citadel and watchtower will become a wasteland forever,
    the delight of donkeys, a pasture for flocks,

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
The fruit of that righteousness will be peace;
    its effect will be quietness and confidence forever.

teaching.name: The Coming King, Tribulation and Spirit

content:
Woe to you, destroyer,
    you who have not been destroyed!
  Woe to you, betrayer,
    you who have not been betrayed!
  When you stop destroying,
    you will be destroyed;
  when you stop betraying,
    you will be betrayed.

The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high;
    he will fill Zion with his justice and righteousness.

The peoples will be burned to ashes;
    like cut thornbushes they will be set ablaze.”

In your thoughts you will ponder the former terror:
    “Where is that chief officer?
  Where is the one who took the revenue?
    Where is the officer in charge of the towers?”

Lord, be gracious to us;
    we long for you.
  Be our strength every morning,
    our salvation in time of distress.

The land dries up and wastes away,
    Lebanon is ashamed and withers;
  Sharon is like the Arabah,
    and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.

The sinners in Zion are terrified;
    trembling grips the godless:
  “Who of us can dwell with the consuming fire?
    Who of us can dwell with everlasting burning?”

Your eyes will see the king in his beauty
    and view a land that stretches afar.

There the Lord will be our Mighty One.
    It will be like a place of broad rivers and streams.
  No galley with oars will ride them,
    no mighty ship will sail them.

You will see those arrogant people no more,
    people whose speech is obscure,
    whose language is strange and incomprehensible.

At the uproar of your army, the peoples flee;
    when you rise up, the nations scatter.

Your plunder, O nations, is harvested as by young locusts;
    like a swarm of locusts people pounce on it.

You who are far away, hear what I have done;
    you who are near, acknowledge my power!

Those who walk righteously
    and speak what is right,
  who reject gain from extortion
    and keep their hands from accepting bribes,
  who stop their ears against plots of murder
    and shut their eyes against contemplating evil—

they are the ones who will dwell on the heights,
    whose refuge will be the mountain fortress.
  Their bread will be supplied,
    and water will not fail them.

Your rigging hangs loose:
    The mast is not held secure,
    the sail is not spread.
  Then an abundance of spoils will be divided
    and even the lame will carry off plunder.

Look, their brave men cry aloud in the streets;
    the envoys of peace weep bitterly.

The highways are deserted,
    no travelers are on the roads.
  The treaty is broken,
    its witnesses are despised,
    no one is respected.

For the Lord is our judge,
    the Lord is our lawgiver,
  the Lord is our king;
    it is he who will save us.

No one living in Zion will say, “I am ill”;
    and the sins of those who dwell there will be forgiven.

All the stars in the sky will be dissolved
    and the heavens rolled up like a scroll;
  all the starry host will fall
    like withered leaves from the vine,
    like shriveled figs from the fig tree.

For the Lord has a day of vengeance,
